title: Quantum Uncertainty and Particle Trajectories: From Heisenberg and Schrödinger to Constructive Dynamical Models
summary: Quantum uncertainty emerged from two strikingly different routes to quantum mechanics. Heisenberg's matrix mechanics replaced the classical description of atomic orbits by relations among observable transition quantities and led, in 1927, to the uncertainty relation and its influential measurement-based interpretation. Schrödinger's wave mechanics grew instead from the Bose--Einstein and de Broglie developments and restored a continuous space-time description through matter waves.
